title: Drums and Euclid
learned: Drums are played by triggers: short pulses that say 'hit now'
A Euclidean pattern spreads HITS as evenly as possible over STEPS
ROTATE shifts a pattern in time without changing it
Each track of the sequencer plays one drum: kick, snare, hat

steps.why: A drum does not need a pitch or a long gate, only a trigger: a short pulse that says 'hit now'. A Euclidean sequencer makes rhythms from two numbers: how many steps, and how many hits spread over them as evenly as possible. Many traditional rhythms from around the world come out this way.
steps.do: In the rack: a clock, a Euclidean sequencer (JX-EUC) with four tracks, and a drum module (JX-DRM) already wired to the console. Press Next.

steps.why: Drum patterns usually run on sixteenth notes.
steps.do: Drag a cable from X4 of the clock to CLOCK of the Euclidean sequencer.
steps.after: All four tracks now step on every sixteenth note. Its PATTERNS display on the front shows where each track hits.

steps.why: Track 1 starts with 4 hits in 16 steps: one on every beat.
steps.do: Drag a cable from GATE 1 of the Euclidean sequencer to KICK TRIG of the drums.
steps.after: A kick drum on every beat: 'four on the floor', the base of house and techno.

steps.why: HITS changes how many hits are spread over the steps.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn HITS of track 1 to 3, then try other numbers.
steps.after: 3 hits in 16 steps cannot be spread evenly, so they fall at 1, 7 and 12: an off-kilter, rolling groove. Go back to 4 for the steady beat.

steps.why: Tracks 2 and 3 have patterns ready for a snare and a hi-hat.
steps.do: Press F2 and drag GATE 2 to SNARE TRIG and GATE 3 to HAT TRIG of the drums.
steps.after: A whole beat: kick on every beat, snare on beats 2 and 4, hats on every eighth note.

steps.why: ROTATE shifts a pattern later in time without changing its spacing.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn ROTATE of track 2.
steps.after: The snare moves away from 2 and 4 and the beat feels different, though it has the same hits. Turn it back to 4 for the classic backbeat.
steps.try: Shape the kit: KICK DECAY makes a short thump or a long boom, SNARE TONE goes from drum body to noise.

steps.do: Steps, hits, rotate: three numbers per drum make a whole beat. Press Next to finish.
